![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062337/assets/e8ff769df4089e6ed9a47d56d7317acf41b8aef6a255abc705c0e7ec31a446ea.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062337/assets/a274b413d20b9aada9f32bc789557097df1a643805c2e8b12c389e3832352c95.png)
e-5470.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
\det(T) = 4 \cdot 2 -  2 \cdot (-1) = 10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,10\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

A triangle $D$ has vertices $(1,1)$, $(4,5),$ and $(-2,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062337/assets/5cb4d5976a3e7153d7041711ab449a1f3af48000021be1d1c4a2c321cbec3467.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062337/assets/ee8f0cf16983d87fa505303ed6372a3f389518d05b3e13f2e9e2121038792b84.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$

$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|-11|\cdot 6 \\  & =66.\end{aligned}
$$

The unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,2\,|\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
